title: Playing at Lufkin's and Oakshire's, tips and pay
summary: Hired Earl Wiggins at a club where he played banjo, got $6 a night plus tips, was fired by the owner, and played at Oakshire's with Johnny Sensei.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: So yeah, speaking about Earl Wiggins, hasn't he got that band at Lufkin's now?

Yeah, well I hired him, you see what I mean? I hired him. Because I was playing piano down there. But the trouble is when I was playing the piano down there, we couldn't get a guitar player nowhere. So what I've done, I hired Wiggins and I played the banjo.
Well he's got a little band there.

So when I told the woman to let me slide a little bit, she fired me. I got a book showing all the little change I made down there, you know. Good, you pick up them, it wasn't much, but then it was better than sitting down, you know what I mean?
Sure, pick up a few tips. You could pick up $20 there in two nights, easy.
Oh that's fine. You know what I mean? I didn't know the tips are all right there.
I didn't know. Oh, tips. You get more tips than the job's paying.
Oh yeah, the job didn't pay much.

No, paying $6, that's all. And then you'd make $6. You'd make $5 if you knew how to hustle, you know what I mean? Go around and people like the music, you know. And she'd have to tell us, you know, slow down on the music, you know. Because I played too fast, nobody's gonna buy no drinks.
You understand what I mean? You just don't play too often.

So that's how we played down there. We played at Oakshire's Place out there with Johnny Sensei and myself. Johnny had an old truck he used to call Caledonia. Yeah, I remember him. So, and now, he said, I know, he said, I'm gonna beat you all the time. And when we looked again, we couldn't see Johnny. Johnny was gone. He was living up there in Jefferson somewhere. Way up in Nettenberg Street. Yeah. Had a little house set back in the yard. Yeah, that's, I can't think of a lot of those guys.
